channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: As atenções agora se voltam para 2028
item.description: Following the 2026 elections, which determined governors, senators, and federal and state representatives, attention in the Brazilian political landscape now turns to the 2028 municipal elections, where mayors and city councilors will be elected. This new electoral cycle promises to bring debates on local governance, security, health, education, and infrastructure in Brazilian cities.

item.title: Flávio espera receber apoio de presidente do União e de deputado estadual mais votado do Rio
item.description: The national president of União Brasil, Antônio de Rueda, is expected to support Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) in the presidential race and Douglas Ruas in the Rio gubernatorial race. The inclusion of Rueda and Márcio Canella on the presidential slate strengthens PL's political network in the Baixada Fluminense, a strategic region for both campaigns.

item.title: Frase do dia
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva claims to be the only anti-system candidate, criticizing the Brazilian Supreme Court for 'promiscuity' in politics. The post includes a poll comparing Lula and Flávio Dino, highlighting debates on corruption and the judiciary.

item.title: “Algumas perdas não têm volta”, diz campanha de Lula
item.description: Lula's campaign released a video highlighting achievements such as the 6X1 work schedule, Popular Pharmacy, minimum wage increases, and pension adjustments while warning about irreversible losses in the 2026 elections. The content targets the runoff against Flávio Bolsonaro, who led in the first round.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula: as propostas dos candidatos à Presidência que disputam o 2º turno
item.description: BBC News Brasil presents an interactive comparison of Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula's proposals for the 2026 presidential runoff, analyzing their stances on economy, security, health, education, environment and other key issues. The content highlights differences between the candidates across areas such as economic policy, public safety and foreign policy, providing contextualized insight for voters.

item.title: Nunes Marques deve liberar revisão criminal de Bolsonaro após 2º turno
item.description: Supreme Federal Court minister Kassio Nunes Marques is expected to review the criminal appeal filed by former president Jair Bolsonaro's defense after the October 25 runoff election. The appeal seeks to suspend Bolsonaro's 27-year sentence for attempted coup, challenging the digital evidence chain. Nunes Marques delayed the decision to avoid influencing the electoral outcome.

item.title: Nova pesquisa testa a disputa Flávio Bolsonaro x Lula no segundo turno pela primeira vez
item.description: AtlasIntel will release on Friday the 9th its first poll on the 2026 presidential runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, measuring voting intention, voter decision-making, candidate rejection, and perceptions in areas like the economy and Supreme Court crisis. The survey maps the direct race between the two, without any other candidates, including questions on governance, political figures, and election dynamics. It will be the first snapshot of the final matchup in the 2026 election.

item.title: Saiba o que os candidatos ao Planalto farão nesta 3ª feira
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian presidential runoff candidates, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), have separate campaign schedules on Tuesday. Lula holds coordination meetings at the Alvorada and Planalto Palaces, while Flávio travels to Goiânia for political meetings with Ronaldo Caiado and Governor Daniel Vilela.

item.title: Agenda de Lula: leia os compromissos do presidente 3ª feira
item.description: President Lula has campaign meetings and encounters with ministers in Brasília on Tuesday, focusing on political and electoral coordination. His agenda includes events at the Alvorada Palace and the Planalto Palace, plus a campaign executive meeting in the afternoon.

item.title: 2026 repete 2022 de forma invertida e direita avança
item.description: The 2026 election mirrors 2022's outcome but with Lula trailing in the first round, reflecting rising anti-petismo and voter fatigue with statist policies. The PT repeats outdated proposals, such as formalizing app drivers with work contracts, failing to grasp the shifting political landscape in Brazil and globally.

item.title: Pesquisas mostravam avanço de Flávio antes do 1º turno
item.description: Pre-election polling data closely matched the actual results of the October 4, 2026, vote, with Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) winning 47.03% and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) receiving 45.16%. Most of nine surveyed firms showed Flávio gaining ground in late September and early October, while Lula held steady and second-tier candidates lost traction.

item.title: Efeito Flávio derruba juro e país economiza R$ 66 bilhões com dívida
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's victory in the first round of the 2026 elections led to a 1 percentage point drop in future interest rates, saving the government R$65.8 billion over four years. The market sees a more fiscally disciplined government under Flávio, allowing more room for interest rate cuts and economic stimulus.

item.title: Lula ou Flávio?
item.description: A poll by Arte/Metrópoles shows 64% of 6,082 readers do not believe Lula could defeat Flávio Dino in a runoff. The hypothetical matchup polarizes opinions on the feasibility of a direct electoral contest between the two leaders.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vs. Lula: o que está em disputa na política energética
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula differ in energy policy: Bolsonaro favors privatization and market logic, while Lula prioritizes sovereignty, energy supply, and transition to a low-carbon economy. The debate reflects contrasting views on the state's role in industry and technology.

item.title: Por que o palhaço Tiririca saiu de cena
item.description: Tiririca, elected in 2010 with 1.3 million votes, saw his support drop 99.6% by 2026, reflecting the decline of Brazilian electoral humor. Known for parodies and few legislative actions, he left PL and joined PSD, promising a more serious mandate. His trajectory symbolizes the wear-out of charismatic figures without legislative effectiveness.

item.title: Bancada do Rio na Câmara dos Deputados é majoritariamente masculina e de direita: dos 46 eleitos, só dez são mulheres
item.description: The Rio de Janeiro state delegation in the Chamber of Deputies remained predominantly male and right-wing, with only 10 women elected out of 46 seats. The Liberal Party (PL) led representation by securing 15 deputies, followed by center and left-wing forces. The election highlighted PL growth and losses for parties like União and Republicanos.

item.title: O anúncio que ligou o sinal de alerta na campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro ainda durante a votação
item.description: The Lula government authorized a PF investigation into alleged U.S. interference in the election, following a Guardian report revealing a project allocating resources to groups critical of the STF. The measure triggered a reaction in Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign during the first-round voting, with polls open. The inquiry was announced by the PF director-general, Andrei Rodrigues.

item.title: Candidatos que usaram ‘Lula’ nas urnas se saem melhor que os que adotaram ‘Bolsonaro’
item.description: Candidates who linked their campaigns to the name 'Lula' performed better electorally than those who used 'Bolsonaro', according to election data analysis. The strategy of invoking influential political figures appears to have positively impacted results.

item.title: ‘Futuro brasileiro é de hegemonia conservadora’, diz Pavanato, deputado federal mais votado em SP
item.description: Lucas Pavanato, the most voted federal deputy in São Paulo, stated that the vote reflects dissatisfaction with the STF and President Lula's government, advocating for conservative hegemony and the impeachment of Alexandre de Moraes. He attributed his high vote count to resistance against the Supreme Court and criticized the Court's actions, referencing the 1932 Constitutional Revolution.

item.title: Antes de braços dados com Lula, Paes agora tenta se distanciar da campanha nacional
item.description: After an unfavorable first-round result in the Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial race, Eduardo Paes seeks to distance himself from Lula's national campaign to avoid alignment with the PT and attract Bolsonaro voters. Allies advocate keeping the local race separate from the presidential contest, especially given Flávio Bolsonaro's strong performance in the state.

item.title: Avanço da direita em eleição no Brasil é vitória de Trump?
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian elections revealed a significant right-wing surge, with victories that may be interpreted as an indirect win for Trump. Foreign analysts question whether this reflects success of his foreign policy toward Latin America. Brazil's conservative shift aligns with the Trumpian agenda.

item.title: Motta tem cenário mais fácil que Alcolumbre para se reeleger no Congresso
item.description: Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB) has a more favorable scenario to retain the presidency of the Chamber of Deputies compared to Davi Alcolumbre's reelection prospects in the Senate, due to the partisan composition of the Chamber. Although the PL leads with 121 deputies, the Centrão maintains control with 234 parliamentarians, ensuring support for Motta. The 2026 presidential election may shape party alliances and legislative strategies.

item.title: Charge do Aroeira
item.description: The cartoon analyzes the post-2022 electoral political dynamic, highlighting Tarcísio de Freitas' victory in São Paulo and the growing conservative wave in Brazil. The content reflects on the limitations of Brazilian presidents regarding established powers and the renewed rivalry between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Dino in upcoming elections.

item.title: Zhongtong chega ao Brasil e quer investir R$ 100 milhões em fábrica de ônibus urbanos
item.description: Chinese bus manufacturer Zhongtong will enter the Brazilian market in 2027, planning to invest R$ 100 million in a factory for electric urban buses, initially through imports. The operation will be conducted in partnership with TEVX, part of Grupo Águia, replicating its successful Chilean model where 900 units are delivered annually. The factory location announcement depends on the October election results.

item.title: ANP oferece maior pacote de áreas do pré-sal desde 2022 em leilão nesta quarta (7)
item.description: The ANP held on Wednesday (7) the largest pre-salt auction since 2022, offering 13 pre-salt blocks and 313 blocks outside the pre-salt, despite protests from environmental organizations against the expansion of oil exploration.

item.title: Flávio e Tarcísio vão a Goiânia fechar apoio de Caiado no 2º turno
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro and Tarcísio de Freitas travel to Goiânia to secure Ronaldo Caiado's support in the 2026 runoff. The meeting follows a call from the candidate to Caiado, who finished fifth in the first round with 2.18% of the votes.

item.title: Daniel Alves declara apoio a Flávio: “Espírito Santo soprou teu nome”
item.description: Daniel Alves, former Brazilian national team player, declared support for senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the second round of the 2026 elections, claiming he received guidance from the “Holy Spirit.” The runoff will be contested between Flávio and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), with Flávio leading polling after the first round. Numerous artists and politicians have already voiced their backing for Flávio, bolstering his support base.

item.title: TSE dá 2 dias para PGE se manifestar sobre recurso de Garotinho
item.description: The TSE gave the PGE 2 days to respond on Garotinho's appeal, who withdrew his requests to nullify his votes. Decision may impact the proclamation of Douglas Ruas as the 1st round winner in Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: Lula diz que “bandidagem cresceu” e Estado não dá conta
item.description: During a campaign meeting for the 2026 runoff election, President Lula stated that states cannot effectively combat organized crime, which has grown into a 'multinational enterprise'. He supports a constitutional amendment allowing federal intervention in public security. Lula received 45.16% in the first round, behind Flávio Bolsonaro's 47.03%.

item.title: Lula destaca abstenção como maior desafio para o 2º turno
item.description: Lula identified voter abstention (21.08%) as the main challenge for the runoff, criticizing Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign and stressing the need for greater electoral engagement. He advocated focusing on correcting campaign errors and exposing threats to democracy.

item.title: Em reunião de campanha, Lula cobra revisão de erros e promete rua
item.description: In a meeting to define 2nd-round strategies, Lula called for reviewing campaign mistakes, focusing on voters who did not vote in the first round. Allies suggested more direct contact with the public through street stops, selfies, and social media. The campaign also prioritized increasing votes in the Northeast and reversing high abstention, which reached 21.08%.

item.title: Lula diz que crise no STF pesa contra sua campanha no 2º turno
item.description: President Lula acknowledged that the STF crisis harms his runoff campaign and proposed a new Judiciary reform to debate minister appointment criteria. After trailing Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round, Lula criticized 'promiscuity' in the Supreme Court and emphasized institutional transparency.

item.title: O que o novo Congresso indica sobre um futuro governo Flávio Bolsonaro ou Lula 4
item.description: The new composition of the National Congress favors a potential Flávio Bolsonaro government, with a more aligned political base through the PL, while a fourth Lula term would face challenges in the Legislative branch.

item.title: A teoria da conspiração sobre as urnas eletrônicas que pode surgir no segundo turno
item.description: The strong performance of the right wing in the first round reduced conspiracy theories about electronic voting machines, but these criticisms may resurface if Lula defeats Flávio Bolsonaro in the second round, according to analysis by José Benedito da Silva.

item.title: A possível entrada na campanha de Lula de personagem que mudou a eleição de 2014
item.description: The potential inclusion of João Santana in Lula's runoff campaign signals a strategic shift, particularly after disappointing first-round results. Santana, known for his 2014 Dilma campaign, may strengthen an offensive approach against Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: SP: Salles teve 120 mil votos, mesmo após desistir da candidatura ao Senado
item.description: Ricardo Salles (Novo) received 120,575 votes for the Senate in São Paulo after withdrawing his candidacy, but all votes were annulled by the court. His withdrawal was approved on October 2nd, but his name remained on the ballots due to the legal deadline of 20 days before the election. After withdrawing, he supported Guilherme Derrite (PP) and André do Prado (PL), who were elected with historical vote records.

item.title: Nunes Marques deve liberar revisão criminal de Bolsonaro para julgamento após segundo turno
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Nunes Marques is expected to rule on the criminal revision requested by Jair Bolsonaro's defense after the electoral runoff, aiming to overturn his conviction for an attempted coup. He delays the decision to avoid influencing the election outcome.

item.title: Lula libera venda de camisetas com marcas de bets que estavam em estoque
item.description: The Secretariat of Social Communication of the Presidency authorized the sale of football shirts already produced with betting house brands, classifying them as 'legacy content' after Provisional Measure 1.394/2026. While sales are allowed, the government warns that using them to promote betting brands will be analyzed by the relevant authorities. The decision responded to a request by Ápice, representing companies such as Adidas, Nike, and Puma, questioning the application of the ban to stock produced before the MP.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro avança na periferia de São Paulo
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) received 42.1% of valid votes in São Paulo in the first round, outperforming his father's 2022 results. Lula (PT) leads the race.

item.title: Renan: “Não espere da gente oposição aguerrida ao Flávio”
item.description: Renan Santos, leader of the Missão party, stated that the party does not intend to strongly oppose a potential government led by Flávio Bolsonaro, citing the PL's performance in the legislative elections. He justified the stance based on political strategy and expressed concerns about possible persecution if the party adopted a more confrontational approach.

item.title: Leia a evolução do número de deputados federais por partido
item.description: In the 2026 election, the PL elected 121 federal deputies, becoming the largest caucus in the Chamber with 23.6% of the 513 seats, surpassing its 2022 performance. Right-wing parties elected 276 deputies, maintaining stability compared to the previous election, while União Brasil led the losses with 13 fewer seats.

item.title: Lula diz carregar “nas costas” a “promiscuidade” do STF
item.description: President Lula said he is 'carrying on his back' the 'promiscuity' of Supreme Court justices, attributing part of his negative result in the first round to the crisis involving court members. He described his candidate as anti-system.

item.title: Fachin diz que STF “permanecerá” após eleição de senadores críticos
item.description: STF President Edson Fachin stated that the Court will remain after the election of critical senators, emphasizing its institutional greatness. He spoke at the Constitution Week event held at the STF Library.

item.title: Sem projetar o futuro, Lula entra no segundo turno com o estigma da ‘fadiga de material’
item.description: Lula advances to the second round at a disadvantage, facing a wave favorable to Flávio Bolsonaro, who appears as the favorite due to the political climate and a national and international environment favorable to the right. The scenario is complex for the PT, with the financial world and the international right celebrating the possibility of Flávio's victory.

item.title: Líderes religiosos que se elegeram em 2026: quem são e para que cargos vão?
item.description: In the 2026 elections, five religious leaders were directly elected to legislative positions: three to state assemblies (one in Goiás and two in Santa Catarina) and two to the Chamber of Deputies (both from Minas Gerais). Additionally, 43 religious leaders were elected as alternates, awaiting potential vacancies. The elected officials represent parties with differing political positions, reflecting the country's ideological diversity.

item.title: ‘Armação do Garotinho com o Douglas Ruas’, diz Paes sobre imbróglio na disputa pelo governo do RJ
item.description: Eduardo Paes accused Anthony Garotinho and Douglas Ruas of orchestrating a scheme to rig the Rio election, suggesting that Garotinho's withdrawal of the appeal at the TSE was a maneuver to nullify his votes and elect Ruas in the first round. The dispute involves the validity of 274,411 votes and potential changes to the election outcome. Paes labeled Garotinho as an 'orange candidate' and criticized the judiciary for not blocking his candidacy.

item.title: Saiba quem assume as vagas de Moro e Cleitinho após senadores serem eleitos para governos estaduais
item.description: Following the 2026 elections, senators elected to state governments will vacate their Senate seats, with their alternates taking over. Alex Diniz and Luis Felipe Cunha will assume the Senate seats for Minas Gerais and Paraná, respectively. Other states like Acre, Amazonas, and Tocantins still await successor definitions.

item.title: O que Lula falou sobre ‘promiscuidade’ do STF após resultado do primeiro turno das eleições
item.description: After the first round, Lula criticized the 'promiscuity' of the STF and proposed judicial reforms, including criteria for minister appointments and fixed terms. He urged allies to increase mobilization and recover absent voters, framing the result as a learning opportunity.

item.title: Entidades europeias veem riscos geopolítico, ambiental e comercial se Flávio Bolsonaro vencer
item.description: European entities express concern over geopolitical, environmental, and commercial risks if Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) wins the 2026 elections, highlighting the troubled legacy of his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro. German newspaper Die Zeit questions how Brazilians reached the first round with a candidate resembling his father, already condemned for environmental violations.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro busca Republicanos para ampliar onda de apoios no 2º turno
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign seeks support from Republicanos to strengthen its base in the second round. The party, led by Marcos Pereira, may boost conservative votes. This movement is part of an alliance strategy to expand support.
